problemStatement.formal: \forall A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}\ \text{of positive upper Banach density},\ \forall p_1,\dots,p_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]\ \text{with}\ p_i(0)=0,\ \exists x,\ \exists d \neq 0:\ x+p_i(d) \in A\ \forall i
problemStatement.plain: Bergelson-Leibman polynomial Szemeredi: every positive-density set of integers contains a polynomial configuration {x + p_i(d)} for any polynomials p_i with no constant term and some d != 0. Recovers Szemeredi (arithmetic progressions) when p_i = i*X.
whyMatters: Strict generalization of Szemeredi's theorem to nonlinear (polynomial) patterns such as {x, x+d^2}
Proved ergodically via polynomial multiple recurrence and the Furstenberg correspondence principle

proven: Statement formalized as a Prop target (combinatorial and ergodic forms); not asserted, 0 axioms
Configuration collapse at d=0 (motivates nondegeneracy d!=0)
p_i(0)=0 <-> X | p_i, hence d | p_i(d): every configuration point = x (mod d)
Linear specialization p_i=i*X recovers the arithmetic progression x+i*d (Szemeredi as degree-one case)
Nonlinear square example {x, x+d^2} with verified perfect-square gap
Poincare single recurrence (k=1 base case) from Mathlib + measure-preservation of polynomial iterates T^{p(n)}
open: Polynomial multiple recurrence for k>=2 (needs PET induction + nilsystem characteristic factors, neither in Mathlib)
Formalize upper Banach density on Z and the density -> configuration implication
